# K4.2 Persistent zeroed grouped-GEMM outputs

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Class: **Fix** (removes non-finite values read as C) · Rule basis: memory placement only; values
equal the upstream path when its memory holds no NaN or Inf.

## 1. Packages

G3, G6 and G6b, where named below, are Firmus's earlier GPT-OSS NVFP4 packages (`nemo_g3_nvfp4_v1`, `nemo_g6_nvfp4_v2`,
`nemo_g6b_nvfp4_v2_1`), withdrawn from this submission and no longer in this repository. Their values, line numbers,
images and test jobs are cited as the record of where evidence was collected ([Index](../KERNELS.md), "Earlier packages").

- `NVFP4_PERSISTENT_GEMM_OUT=1` (config line 127); same in G3, G6, G6b, G6c.
- Code: `transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` → `transformer_engine/pytorch/ops/fused/grouped_mlp.py`,
  byte-identical. The G6/G6b/G6c V7 patch also modifies `grouped_mlp.py` but not these lines.

## 2. What the reference does

TE's CuTe fused grouped MLP allocates the FC2 forward output and the FC1 dgrad output with `torch.empty` (via
`validate_or_alloc_output`) and runs cuBLASLt grouped GEMM with a per-group beta held on the device. With beta = 0
cuBLAS still reads C, which aliases the output, so stale NaN gives `0 × NaN = NaN` (patch comments L2111–2112,
L2471).

## 3. What this implementation does

`_finite_grouped_gemm_out(role, buffer, shape, dtype, device)` (L1595–1611) replaces both allocations (FC2 fprop
L2113–2115, FC1 dgrad L2472–2474):
- switch on and no caller buffer: one buffer per `(role, shape, dtype, device)`, created with `torch.zeros` on first
  use and returned on every later call (L1602–1608), shared by every layer of that shape;
- otherwise: the caller's buffer or a new one, zero-filled on every call (L1609–1610).

With K4.3 the shapes are fixed, so all NVFP4 MoE layers share one FC2-output and one FC1-dgrad buffer.

## 4. Why the result is the same

The GEMM computes \(D = \alpha AB + \beta C\) with \(\beta = 0\). With finite C, \(\beta C = \pm 0\) and \(D = \alpha AB\),
except that an exactly zero \(\alpha AB\) can take its sign from C (\(-0 + {+0} = +0\)); the upstream path, reading
uninitialized memory, has the same dependence. The buffer starts at 0 and later holds earlier GEMM outputs, which
are finite unless a GEMM itself produced a non-finite value. Reuse is valid only if each output is consumed before
the same role's GEMM runs again (docstring L1596–1600): FC2's output by the unpermute of the same layer's forward
(K3.4), FC1 dgrad's by the permute backward of the same layer. For FC2 this order is enforced indirectly: each FC2
output carries a deferred bias keyed by the buffer pointer, and the next deferral raises if the previous one was not
consumed (L3588–3589). **Class: Fix**; active rows equal the zero-fill path.

## 5. Numerics

No arithmetic change. Rows that no GEMM writes (none in the K4.3 layout, see K4.1) keep earlier finite values
instead of zeros.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** `buffer is None and _PERSISTENT_GEMM_OUT` (L1602), read once at import (L1510).
- **Falls back:** a caller-supplied buffer or the switch off gives a zero fill per call (L1609–1610): also finite,
  one extra memset. Silent.
- **Assumes:** (a) no consumer reads an FC2 output or FC1 dgrad after the next GEMM of the same role and shape
  (nothing checks this for FC1 dgrad); (b) no consumer reads rows past the used rows; (c) the buffers stay alive
  across CUDA-graph capture and replay (module-level dict L1513).
- **Check:** the config line above; no log line. Scored runs: no NaN loss, 10 `run_stop` `success` per package.

## 7. Code

`transformer_engine_firmus_nvfp4.patch` → `grouped_mlp.py`: switch L1510, buffer dict L1513, `_finite_grouped_gemm_out`
L1595–1611, FC2 fprop L2111–2115, FC1 dgrad L2471–2474. Applied by `Dockerfile` L113.

## 8. Tests and evidence

Jobs: this package's image: 22907/22908, 22913, 22891, 22887, 22920/22921 (results at the end of this section); the bullets below are the G6 image's (22437, 22500, 22478, 22494, 22348).

- **`k4_k5_9_grouped_mlp`**, persistent vs zero fill, allocator prefilled with 0xFF: 0 non-finite y and dx. 3.7·10⁶
  (real routing) to about 3·10⁷ (all tokens on one expert) elements differ; job 22228 placed every differing row past
  the used rows (the test's tail, not produced by K4.3), active and padding rows 0. Fixture `torch.empty` C:
  19 595 264 non-finite (y and dx). Control zero fill vs itself: 43–45 elements (dprobs, bias gradients).
- **`k4_2_cross_layer`** (two modules sharing the buffers): sequential, seeded: about 7.7·10⁵ elements differ, the first
  layer's 0 and the second layer's y and dx 385 664 / 385 663 (job 22500); weight gradients 0. The
  second layer sees rows the first left behind; which rows was not read. Interleaved forward/forward/backward/backward without consuming the output raises
  `AttributeError` in TE's saved-tensor restore (the 2 recorded errors per run); with the output consumed after each
  forward, as the unpermute does, the counts equal the sequential case.
- **`k4_2_replay_vs_probe`** (G6 training capture, graph replay vs eager forward of the same layer): 27 of 28 equal;
  iteration 303, layer 1 (FP8 attention, K8.1, not run-to-run deterministic) 2682 elements.
- **`k4_2_bwd_graph_vs_eager`** (same capture, backward): layer 23 differs as much as eager vs eager; layers 0 and 11
  differ in almost every element (about 1.45·10⁸), also with cloned inputs (jobs 22485, 22492). Not explained.
- **`k7_3_k4_2_graph`** (module captured with `make_graphed_callables`, persistent buffer is the graph output):
  replay vs eager y differs in all active rows before backward (296 921 346 elements) and dx has 5 275 648
  non-finite tail elements; zero fill differs only in dprobs (the test passes probs twice, doubling dprobs). Not
  explained (jobs 22341, 22348).

This package's image (modules built as this package's model where `../KERNELS.md` section 9 says so):

- `k4_k5_9_grouped_mlp`, jobs 22907 / 22908: 140 cases, 106 with a difference per run (K4.1).
- `k4_2_cross_layer`, job 22913 (`../KERNELS.md` section 9): 8 cases, 8 with a difference, 2 recorded errors per run (the
  interleaved forward/forward/backward/backward case, as above); run a vs b 1,054 digests equal, 18 differ.
- `k4_2_replay_vs_probe`, job 22891 (inputs captured from this package's training run, job 22873): 14 cases, 0 with
  a difference; run a vs b 14 equal.
- `k4_2_bwd_graph_vs_eager`, job 22887 (same capture): 18 cases, 16 with a difference. The NVFP4 layers 0, 1, 11,
  12 and 21 (iterations 4 and 303) differ in 12 of 12 outputs, 1.25·10⁸–1.46·10⁸ elements; the MXFP8 tail layers 22
  and 23 differ in 6 of 12 outputs, 64,298–107,260 elements, where their eager-vs-eager control differs in 3–5
  outputs, 222–14,192 elements. Run a vs b: 216 equal, 0 differ. Not explained, as on the G6 image.
- `k7_3_k4_2_graph`, jobs 22920 / 22921 (`../KERNELS.md` section 9): 35 cases, 24 with a difference, 2 recorded errors
  per run; run a vs b 845 equal, 15 differ.

## 9. Open points

1. The `k7_3_k4_2_graph` persistent-buffer result and the layer 0 / 11 backward differences are unexplained. In
   training the buffers are consumed inside the layer's graph and are not graph outputs; that difference from the
   test is an argument, not a measurement.
2. Assumption (a) for FC1 dgrad (and that FC2's output is not saved for backward) rests on TE's fused-op autograd,
   which is not quoted here.
